svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Windup is not a fault of the integrator. It is what an integrator does to an open loop.
While the actuator sits on its limit the feedback path is cut, and the integrator keeps integrating an error it can no longer affect
(b) how far outside the limit the demand went
(a) On the limit the actuator output stops following its input, so nothing the controller does reaches the hull and the error cannot change sign.
The violet path is the only addition either anti-windup scheme makes. It carries the difference between demand and delivery, which is
identically zero while the actuator follows — so an unsaturated loop cannot tell whether anti-windup is fitted.
(b) The characteristic drawn to scale. Section F measured a peak demand of 3480 N against a limit of 239.36 N: an overdraft of 14.5 times.
